definition: An attack that attempts to determine whether a specific data point was part of a model's training dataset.
details: Membership inference attacks are a privacy concern for models trained on sensitive data, and defenses like differential privacy are designed in part to mitigate this risk.
story: Imagine a new medicine that works brilliantly in the lab but still has to be tested on real people before anyone takes it. In plain words: An attack that attempts to determine whether a specific data point was part of a model's training dataset. Here is how it actually plays out: Membership inference attacks are a privacy concern for models trained on sensitive data, and defenses like differential privacy are designed in part to mitigate this risk. Rules and red-teaming are the brakes that make the speed trustworthy. That deliberate caution is Membership Inference Attack.
